subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation for Acme Payments

Ethan — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I’ve kept this focused on reliability / graceful degradation since that was your primary concern.

Pain points you shared
- Recent incidents where your inference endpoint experienced regional capacity shortages causing 10–30s tail latency and a spike in 5xx errors (noted in Mar/Apr).
- Lack of automated fallback to alternate regions or lighter-weight model variants; SREs currently perform manual failover.
- Customer-facing SLAs require 99.9% availability and p95 latency targets that are being missed during peak settlement windows.
- Cost sensitivity around running 24/7 dedicated capacity for peak traffic.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Primary inference hosted in GCP us-central with autoscaling managed by in-house orchestrator.
- Using a mixture of in-house models and a third-party transformer model for data enrichment.
- Logging: Splunk for traces, BigQuery for aggregated metrics.

Success criteria you outlined
1) Reliable automatic failover to alternate region or model variant with minimal recovery time (<= 30s for circuit-break + fallback).
2) Predictable p95 latency under 99th percentile traffic spikes.
3) Visibility: token-level cost and latency breakdown per route for cost attribution.
4) Clear operational playbooks + audit logs for compliance.

Summary of what Redwood can bring (high level)
- Smart routing: automatic policy-based routing by latency/cost/region with transparent fallback to compatible model variants.
- Graceful degradation: configurable model tiers (full -> quantized -> embed-only) and region failover with KV cache warmup strategies to reduce cold-starts.
- Observability: per-route dashboards, token-level cost, and tracing hooks; can integrate with Splunk/BigQuery.
- Dedicated & Private options if you prefer reserved capacity or VPC isolation for settlement workloads.

Attachments: Redwood-Mutual-Action-Plan.docx (draft MAP with suggested milestones & roles).

Proposed next steps
- You to share the incident summary and any SRE postmortems (if possible).
- Redwood to propose a short pilot (2–3 weeks): 
  * Phase 1: Synthetic load validation + failover testing to a secondary region.
  * Phase 2: Small production canary (non-critical route) with monitoring + rollback policy.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your SREs to walk through routing/fallback options (30–45m).

Availability: I’m free Wed/Thu this week (PDT). Marissa (cc’d) will coordinate the tech call.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@acmepayments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acmepayments.com>, Acme Payments SRE Team <sre@acmepayments.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation for Acme Payments

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and I’ve attached the incident summary from our April outage for context.

Incident highlights (from the attached PDF)
- 2026-04-12: US-central GPU pool exhausted during peak settlement; autoscaler lag + long queueing resulted in p95 latency > 15s and ~0.8% 5xx across affected routes.
- Manual failover to eu-west was initiated by SREs; due to model size mismatch and cold KV caches, end-to-end recovery took ~5 minutes and caused degraded responses.
- No automatic downgrade to lighter model variants configured; we’d like an automatic path that reduces quality slightly but keeps latency within SLA.

Constraints
- Compliance: any cross-region fallback must remain within contractual data residency boundaries for certain merchant data.
- Budget: prefer to avoid a large always-on reserved fleet unless we can demonstrate clear savings vs. ad-hoc cloud bursts.

Happy to run the pilot but need a clear risk plan for data residency and a rollback path. Can share access to the incident postmortem and a small sample of traces (redacted).

Proposed times: Wed 2026-05-20 10:00–11:00 PDT for the SRE deep-dive. Jenna will confirm.

Attachment: Acme_SRE-incident-summary.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation for Acme Payments — internal notes

Ben — quick internal note after reading Ethan’s incident summary. Key asks we should prioritize for the pilot:
- Automated fallback plan: define model-tier mapping (full -> int8 quantized -> lightweight embed-only) and exact quality tradeoffs.
- Region failover: validate KV cache pre-warm approach and warm-start latency expectations (include mock runbook).
- Data residency: we need to confirm whether we can route only metadata across regions while keeping PII in primary region; security team will need to sign off.

I attached an updated Mutual Action Plan with proposed milestones, owners, and a preliminary SLA/rollback clause. I also added a pricing option for a small reserved baseline + burstable capacity — should address their cost concerns.

Attachment: Redwood-Mutual-Action-Plan.docx

If you want, I can take point on the SRE deep-dive and present the fallback playbook. Jonas can cover kernel/quantization options.

—Marissa

- 10m: Acme incident summary walk-through (Ethan)
- 15m: Redwood proposed fallback architecture (Marissa) — model tiers, region routing, cache warmup, rollback flows
- 10m: Open Q&A + next steps (pilot scope & timelines)

Links: https://hubspot.company.com/deal/4491 | https://app.redwood.ai/mutual-action/DEAL-4491
